title: Eye labelling sheet
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 23 (Eye labelling sheet (portal worksheet, printable or on a drawing tablet))
intro: Lesson 23: Cameras and eyes. To understand how the eye and camera use a lens to focus an image

picture.alt: A labelled diagram of the eye
picture.draw: Draw and label: Eye labelling sheet

questions.q: In bright light the pupil gets smaller. Which part causes this?
questions.model: Which part controls the pupil? The iris. In bright light it narrows the pupil, letting in less light to protect the retina.

questions.q: Which part of a camera does the job of the retina?
Why is a pinhole camera image upside down?
questions.a: Rays travel in straight lines and cross at the pinhole.

questions.q: Core: Label the eye diagram and write the job of each part.
questions.a: As in the table: cornea, iris, pupil, lens, retina, optic nerve.
questions.model: Teacher labels the cornea first: 'clear front layer, bends light as it enters'.

questions.q: Extend: Make a pinhole camera (box, foil with a pinhole, tracing paper screen). Look at a bright window and describe the image.
questions.a: Image is upside down, dim and small; a bigger hole makes it brighter but blurrier.

questions.q: Stretch: Explain how the eye focuses on near and far objects.
questions.a: Ciliary muscles change the lens shape: fatter for near, thinner for far.

questions.q: The image on the retina is...
Big question: how is your eye like a camera, and how is it better?
questions.a: Both focus light with a lens onto a detector; the eye changes focus quickly and the brain processes images.
